morgan: Heads-up — noticed token-level drift when restoring KV-snapshots during a mid-generation rollforward on the int4 canary (magnet-16b-int4).

jess: ugh, can you paste the minimal repro?

morgan: Repro steps: start generation -> trigger canary fallback to older shard -> take KV snapshot -> kill connection -> restore snapshot and continue. Drift shows up ~120 tokens after restore. Logs attached: `self_attn_qk_norm` spikes.

kai: interesting. is it RoPE phase mismatch or index offset?

morgan: initial hypothesis: phase scale mismatch because we apply a micro-quantized kernel during rollforward that uses a different rotation normalization.

sanjay: can you paste the log excerpt? small snippets enough.

morgan: ```
[2026-07-12 14:02:11] gen@shard-3: kv_restore: snapshot_id=abcd1234, seq=1048576
[2026-07-12 14:02:11] gen@shard-3: kernel=attn_qkv_int4_opt_v2, rot_scale=0.9987
[2026-07-12 14:02:12] gen@shard-3: self_attn_qk_norm avg=0.0021 -> 0.0189 after restore
```

jess: rot_scale change is tiny but could accumulate with long context. Was the snapshot taken with the same kernel?

morgan: snapshot was from `attn_qkv_int4_opt_v1` (older), then on restore we've been routing to opt_v2 because of routing policy that prefers v2 for throughput.

kai: aha. so KV layout is fine but the rotation normalization semantics differ. That would cause RoPE phase offsets for keys in cache.

perf-bot: [perf-bot] Canary deviation > 0.5% perplexity for longprefill sequences. Ticket auto-created: INF-7421.

sanjay: can we force kernel consistency on restore as quick mitigation? e.g., pin the kernel in the snapshot metadata and prefer fallback to original variant.

morgan: I tried forcing `kernel_hint=opt_v1` at restore and drift disappears in 3 reproductions.

jess: good quickfix. Long term we need a compatibility matrix and a validation that snapshots carry kernel ABI/hash and that runtime rejects incompatible kernel(semantics).

kai: agree. also add a unit that runs a short continuation after restoring to check self-attn QK stats within delta. If mismatch -> fallback to CPU-serial restore or mark snapshot stale.

morgan: wrote a tiny smoke script: `scripts/repro_rope_restore.sh` with steps and asserts. Pushed to canary branch `fix/kv-restore-kernel-check`.

sanjay: can you add the log assertion to the rollout gate? If perf-bot flags drift we should block canary.

morgan: will add the `self_attn_qk_norm` check to the rollout hook. Patch in PR #4291.

jess: also run the quant-eval suite (longprefill goldset) under both opt_v1 and opt_v2 kernels and diff outputs to produce a small fingerprint. Put results in the onboarding matrix.

kai: I'll run the longflight harness overnight (48h) against magnet16k and magnet-16b-int4 to surface edge drift.

morgan: thanks. for triage: owner=morgan, blocker=canary until we land kernel ABI checks, next steps listed in INF-7421.

jess: :thumbsup: any quick mitigation for customers on Dedicated?

sanjay: add a server-side flag to force restore kernel affinity per-customer until we publish compatibility guarantees.

morgan: filed a small ops request with eng-infra: "restore-kernel-affinity toggle".

perf-bot: [perf-bot] INF-7421 updated: status=triage, assignees=[morgan], priority=P1.

jess: great. keep notes about token lag window where drift appears (approx 100-140 tokens post-restore) so QA can craft focused tests.

kai: logging TODO: include `rot_scale` and `rot_epoch` in snapshot manifest.

morgan: adding that to the PR too. I'll post a short follow-up with links to the repro logs and the branch.

jess: thanks — we'll try not to route restores to mismatched kernels until ABI is stable.

morgan: update: quick rollback landed on canary, drift no longer seen in 4/4 retries. will keep monitoring.

(ended)
